column2: 中古英语 string ← 古英语 strenġ（绳、弦）← 原始日耳曼语 *strangiz（绳）← 原始印欧语 *strengʰ-（绳索；收紧）
column3: a thin cord used for tying things
column5: He tied the parcel with string.|A string of small islands lay offshore.
column6: a thin length that ties or links things together – 细长的一条，用来系住或把东西串起来
column7: 细绳：比线粗、比绳细的那种|弦：乐器上绷紧的那一条，同是细长绷直之物|一串：把东西沿一条线连起来，故称一串

column2: 英语 strip 或为 stripe 的变体，或 ← 中古低地德语 strippe，更早词源不明；动词「剥去」一支 ← 古英语 strīepan（掠夺）← 原始日耳曼语 *strēpōną
column3: a long narrow piece of something, or to pull off an outer layer
column5: Cut the paper into narrow strips.|He stripped the old paint from the door.
column6: a long narrow piece, or the taking of one off – 长而窄的一条，或把这样一层揭下来
column7: 条带：长而窄的一片|剥去：把贴在表面的一层揭掉|脱下：把身上穿着的一层去掉

column2: 中古英语 stripe ← 中古荷兰语／中古低地德语 strîpe（条纹）← 原始西日耳曼语 *strīpā ← 原始日耳曼语 *strīpô
column3: a long band of colour different from the surface around it
column5: The shirt has blue and white stripes.|A tiger's stripes help it hide in grass.
column6: a long band of colour running across a surface – 一道颜色不同的长带横过表面
column7: 条纹：人为织出或画上的长带|斑纹：动物身上天生的那种长带

column2: 英语 strive ← 古法语 estriver（争、竞）← 法兰克语 *strīban（使力、奋争）；与 strife 同支
column3: to make great efforts to achieve something
column5: She strove to finish before dark.|They strive for higher standards each year.
column6: pushing hard against what stands in the way – 顶着阻力一直往前使劲
column7: 努力：持续使力去做|力争：使力的方向是争到某个结果

column2: 中古英语 strok ← 古英语 strāc ← 原始日耳曼语 *straikaz（一击、一抹）← 原始印欧语 *streyg-（抚、擦、击）
column3: a single movement of a brush, pen, or hand across a surface
column5: He finished the painting with a few strokes.|Her father died after a stroke.
column6: one continuous movement across a surface – 沿表面走过的一趟连续动作
column7: 一笔：笔在纸面走过一趟|击打：手或器物落到物上那一下|中风：脑内血管突然出事，像被猛击一下，故借此名

column2: 借自德语 strollen，是瑞士德语 strolchen（游荡）的变体 ← Strolch（流浪汉）
column3: to walk slowly for pleasure, without hurrying
column5: They strolled along the river after supper.|We took a stroll through the market.
column6: walking at an easy pace with nowhere to be – 不赶时间地慢慢走
column7: 散步：为舒展身心而慢走|闲逛：走着看着，没有固定去处

column2: 中古英语 strong ← 古英语 strang（强的）← 原始西日耳曼语 *strang（严的、强的）← 原始印欧语 *strengʰ-（绷紧、硬）
column3: having great power, or hard to break or move
column5: He is strong enough to lift the crate alone.|She likes her coffee strong.
column6: able to put out or take great force – 能发出大力，也能受住大力
column7: 强壮的：人身上力气大|坚固的：物体受力也不坏|浓的：味道或成分厚重，作用得强

column2: 中古英语 struglen，更早词源不明；或为 *strokelen 的变体 ← 中古荷兰语 struyckelen（绊跌）← 原始日耳曼语 *strūkōną（发僵、跌绊）
column3: to try hard to do something difficult, often while failing
column5: He struggled up the wet rock face.|Many families struggle to pay the rent.
column6: straining against something that keeps pushing back – 顶着一直把你推回来的东西使劲
column7: 挣扎：身体使力想脱出困境|奋斗：把这份使力拉长成一段长期的努力|难以应付：使了力仍显吃力，进展有限

column2: 中古英语 stiborne，更早词源不明；一说 ← 古英语 *stybbor ← stybb（树桩）＋ 形容词后缀 -or，取树桩钉在地里不动之意
column3: refusing to change one's mind or give way
column4: 固执的/顽固的/难去除的
column5: He is too stubborn to admit a mistake.|That stain proved stubborn despite three washes.
column6: planted so firmly that nothing shifts it – 扎在那里，怎么推都不移
column7: 固执的：主意定死，不听劝|顽固的：抗拒改变的程度更重|难去除的：污渍或毛病赖着不走，同是不肯移

column2: 中古英语 student ← 古法语 estudiant ← 拉丁语 studens，是 studeō（专心从事、钻研）的现在分词
column3: a person who is learning at a school or university
column5: She is a student at the local college.|The class has thirty students.
column6: one whose present business is to learn – 眼下的本分就是学的那个人
column7: 学生：在学校里受教的人|学员：受训于某项课程或技能的人

column2: 借自意大利语 studio（书房、画室）← 拉丁语 studium（专心、钻研）；与 study 同源
column3: a room where an artist works or where recordings are made
column5: The painter rented a studio near the harbour.|The band recorded in a small studio.
column6: a room set aside for making something – 专腾出来做东西的那个房间
column7: 工作室：供人创作或制作的房间|画室：专用于绘画的那种|演播室：供录音录影的那种

column2: 中古英语 studien ← 古法语 estudier ← 拉丁语 studium（热忱、专心钻研）
column3: to spend time learning about a subject
column5: She studies medicine in Edinburgh.|He studied the map before setting out.
column6: putting sustained attention on something to understand it – 把注意力长时间放在一事上，为的是弄懂
column7: 学习：为掌握而反复用心|研究：用心的程度更深，要弄出结论|书房：专供这件事用的房间

column2: 中古英语 stuf ← 古法语 estofe（材料、装备）← estoffer（备齐、填塞）← 古高地德语 stoffōn ← 原始西日耳曼语 *stoppōn（堵塞、填满）
column3: things of various kinds, or material of some sort
column5: Move your stuff off the table.|The chair is stuffed with horsehair.
column6: whatever fills a space, named without naming it – 占着地方的那些，懒得一一点名就这么说
column7: 杂物：说不清也不必细分的那些物件|材料：做东西所用的料|填塞：把料塞进空处，本义正在此

column2: 英语 stumble 终究出自原始日耳曼语 *stam-（绊住、结舌）；与德语 stumm（哑的）、荷兰语 stom（哑的）相关，与 stammer 同源
column3: to catch the foot on something and almost fall
column5: He stumbled on a loose stone.|I stumbled across an old photo in the drawer.
column6: the foot catching so the body loses its footing – 脚被挂住，身子一时失了重心
column7: 绊倒：脚被挂住而跌|失足：踩空或踏错这一下|偶然碰上：像走路被挂住一样，不期然遇到某物

column2: 中古英语 stonen ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 estoner（击昏、震住）← 晚期拉丁语 *stunāre ← 法兰克语 *stunōn（雷鸣、轰响）；另一说 ← 古英语 stunian（轰击）
column3: to make someone unable to think or react, by a blow or by shock
column5: The blow stunned him for a moment.|The news stunned everyone in the office.
column6: a jolt so hard that the mind stops working – 一下震得厉害，脑子一时不转
column7: 使昏迷：击打使人失去知觉|使震惊：消息使人一时反应不过来

column2: 源自中古法语 stupide ← 拉丁语 stupidus（被击得发懵的）← stupeō（发懵、惊愕）← 原始印欧语 *(s)tewp-（顶、撞）
column3: showing a lack of thought or good sense
column5: It was stupid to leave the door unlocked.|He felt stupid for asking twice.
column6: acting as if the mind were knocked blank – 像被撞懵了一样不加思量
column7: 愚蠢的：判断上明显失当|笨的：反应慢、学得慢

column2: 中古英语 sturdy（悍勇的、倔强的）← 古法语 estourdi（被打晕的）← estourdir（打晕）← 通俗拉丁语 *exturdire，更早词源不明
column3: strongly built and not easily damaged
column5: The table stood on four sturdy legs.|She wore sturdy boots for the hike.
column6: built solid enough to take rough use – 做得实，经得住折腾
column7: 结实的：物件用料足、不易坏|坚固的：结构受力也不变形|健壮的：人身板厚实、经得住

column2: 中古英语 stile（书写工具；表达方式）← 古法语 estile／中世纪拉丁语 stylus ← 拉丁语 stilus（尖笔；文风）← 原始印欧语 *(s)teyg-（尖、刺）
column3: the particular way in which something is done or made
column5: His prose has a plain, direct style.|That coat is out of style now.
column6: the recognisable way one does a thing – 做一件事时那种一眼能认出的做法
column7: 风格：作者或时代特有的那种做法|式样：具体的形制与款式|时尚：某段时间里流行的那种式样

column2: 由 sub-（在下）＋ marine（海的）构成；marine 一支 ← 古法语 marin ← 拉丁语 marinus ← mare（海）
column3: a ship that can travel under water
column5: The submarine dived below the ice.|They laid a submarine cable across the strait.
column6: a vessel that travels below the surface – 在水面以下航行的船
column7: 潜艇：能潜到水下航行的舰船|水下的：位于或用于水面以下的

column2: 中古英语 substancial ← 古法语 substanciel ← 拉丁语 substantialis ← substantia（实体）← substō（立于其下、支撑）
column3: large in amount, or having real weight and solidity
column5: They made a substantial profit last year.|There is no substantial difference between the two.
column6: having enough weight behind it to count – 分量够，压得住
column7: 大量的：数量或金额可观|实质的：不是表面，是真有内容的那部分|结实的：物件本身厚实牢固

column2: 中古英语 sotil ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 sotel／古法语 sotil ← 拉丁语 subtilis（细密的、精细的），原指织得细的布 ← sub（在下）＋ tela（织物）
column3: so slight or delicate that it is not easy to notice
column5: There is a subtle difference in the shade.|She gave a subtle hint about the cost.
column6: so fine that it slips past a first look – 细到头一眼看不出来
column7: 细微的：差别小到要留心才觉|精妙的：处理得精细，见功夫|含蓄的：话不明说，留在字面之下

column2: 源自古法语 suburbe ← 拉丁语 suburbium，由 sub-（在下、靠近）＋ urbs（城）构成
column3: a residential area on the edge of a city
column5: They moved to a quiet suburb last year.|Trains run from the suburbs every ten minutes.
column6: the ring of housing that sits just outside the city proper – 紧贴城区之外那一圈住宅地带
column7: 郊区：城外供居住的地带|近郊：其中离城较近的那一带

column2: 由 sub-（在下）＋ way（路）构成；way 一支 ← 古英语 weġ（路）← 原始日耳曼语 *wegaz
column3: an underground railway, or a tunnel for pedestrians to cross under a road
column5: She takes the subway to work.|Use the subway to reach the other platform.
column6: a way that runs below the ground – 走在地面以下的通路
column7: 地铁：在地下行驶的铁路|地下通道：供人从路面之下穿过的通路

column2: 中古英语 souken ← 古英语 sūcan（吸）← 原始西日耳曼语 *sūkan ← 原始印欧语 *sewg-（吸）
column3: to draw liquid into the mouth by using the lips and tongue
column5: The baby sucked milk from the bottle.|He sucked the juice up through a straw.
column6: drawing something in by making the space inside emptier – 把里面抽空，东西就被带进来
column7: 吸：靠口内减压把液体引入|吮：含着慢慢吸，动作更轻缓|很差：口语里说某事糟糕，用的是这个词的另一层引申

column2: 中古英语 sodeyn ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 sodein ← 古法语 sodain ← 通俗拉丁语 *subitanus ← 拉丁语 subitaneus ← subitus（悄然而至的）← subeō（悄悄靠近）
column3: happening quickly and without warning
column5: A sudden gust slammed the door shut.|His sudden departure surprised everyone.
column6: arriving with no warning at all – 一点预兆也没有就到了
column7: 突然的：事情来得没有铺垫|骤然的：变化来得又快又猛

column2: 中古英语 suffisen ← 中古法语 souffire ← 拉丁语 sufficiō（供得上、够用），由 sub（在下）＋ faciō（做）构成
column3: to be enough for a purpose
column5: One lamp will suffice for this desk.|A brief note should suffice.
column6: being just enough to meet the need – 刚好够上所需，不必更多
column7: 足够：数量或程度够用|满足需要：正好把所需的填上

column2: 中古英语 sugre ← 古法语 sucre ← 中世纪拉丁语 succarum ← 阿拉伯语 sukkar ← 波斯语 shakar ← 梵语 sharkara（砂粒、砂糖）
column3: a sweet substance obtained from cane or beet, used to sweeten food
column5: He takes two spoons of sugar in his tea.|Sugar dissolves faster in hot water.
column6: sweet grains that melt into whatever they are stirred through – 甜的细粒，搅进什么就化在什么里
column7: 糖：那种甜味物质的通称|砂糖：呈细粒状的那种|加糖：把它放进饮食里这个动作

column2: 英语 suicide ← 新拉丁语 suicidium，由 sui（自己的，反身代词属格）＋ -cidium（杀）构成，1643 年始见于 Thomas Browne 笔下
column3: the act of killing oneself
column5: The charity runs a suicide prevention line.|Cutting research funding would be economic suicide.
column6: the taking of one's own life – 结束自己性命这件事
column7: 自杀：字面义，自己结束自己的命|自毁之举：把这层用在事情上，指自取灭亡的做法

column2: 中古英语 sulphur ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 sulfre ← 拉丁语 sulfur，更早词源不明；取代了古英语 swefl
column3: a yellow non-metal element that burns with a blue flame and a sharp smell
column5: Sulfur burns with a pale blue flame.|The spring water smelled of sulfur.
column6: a brittle yellow element with a sharp burning smell – 脆的黄色元素，烧起来气味刺鼻
column7: 硫：作为化学元素的名称|硫磺：这种元素的天然块状或粉状形态

column2: 中古英语 somer ← 古英语 sumor ← 原始日耳曼语 *sumaraz ← 原始印欧语 *semh₂-（夏）
column3: the warmest season of the year, between spring and autumn
column5: We spent the summer by the sea.|Summer comes late this far north.
column6: the warmest stretch of the year – 一年里最热的那一段
column7: 夏天：日常说法，指那段时节|夏季：把它当四季之一来说，多用于书面
